entity.summary: Long-running self-custody Ethereum and multichain wallet ecosystem offering mobile, browser and web-based tools.
entity.notes: MEW's first-party ten-year history dates the original Ether Wallet Generator to 2015-08-11. This batch models the current MEW Mobile product separately from the broader entity lineage.

products.summary: Current MEW mobile wallet application for iOS and Android, providing self-custody wallet access and onchain features.
products.notes: Current product identity is first-party supported; initial MEW Mobile launch date is intentionally unresolved in this batch.

events.title: BGP and DNS hijack redirected MyEtherWallet web users to a phishing site
events.description: A BGP route hijack affecting Amazon Route 53 DNS infrastructure redirected some DNS resolution for myetherwallet.com to a malicious server. Users who proceeded through the invalid TLS certificate warning could submit wallet credentials to the phishing site, and the attacker used stolen information to transfer Ethereum.
events.notes: The incident is scoped to the public web/DNS path rather than a compromise of MEW application code or wallet servers. MEW stated that its Chrome extension and locally run/offline copies were not affected. Cloudflare's network analysis attributes the hijacked DNS routes to Amazon Route 53; WLR does not preserve the early Google-DNS attribution from the initial MEW statement. No exact loss amount is canonicalized in this candidate.

evidence.title: 10 Years of MyEtherWallet: Evolving with Ethereum
evidence.notes: First-party history dates the original Ether Wallet Generator to August 11, 2015 and preserves continuity into MyEtherWallet.

evidence.title: MyEtherWallet: An Introduction
evidence.notes: First-party current overview identifies MEW Mobile for iOS and Android and states that MEW remains non-custodial, open-source and client-side.

evidence.title: Official statement regarding DNS spoofing of MyEtherWallet domain
evidence.notes: MEW's official incident statement says its domain's public DNS path was hijacked and users were redirected to a phishing site. Follow-up statements from the MEW team say the Chrome extension and locally run copies were not affected.

evidence.title: BGP leaks and cryptocurrencies
evidence.notes: Cloudflare's first-hand BGP and DNS-resolver analysis attributes the hijacked prefixes to Amazon Route 53 DNS, observes malicious responses specifically for myetherwallet.com, and reports that stolen login information was used to transfer Ethereum.
